items.text: Michael W. Frerichs was elected Illinois State Treasurer in 2014 and is in his third term. He is the state's Chief Investment and Banking Officer and actively manages approximately $60 billion. He also serves as vice chair of the Illinois State Board of Investment, which manages approximately $28.6 billion in pension and trust assets. Before becoming treasurer, he was a Democratic state senator for east-central Illinois and served as Champaign County Auditor.

sentences.text: Michael W. Frerichs was elected Illinois State Treasurer in 2014 and is in his third term.
He is the state's Chief Investment and Banking Officer and actively manages approximately $60 billion.
He also serves as vice chair of the Illinois State Board of Investment, which manages approximately $28.6 billion in pension and trust assets.
Before becoming treasurer, he was a Democratic state senator for east-central Illinois and served as Champaign County Auditor.

items.text: His office made $1.5 billion in investment earnings on the state portfolio in 2025. During his time in office, state investment earnings have exceeded $5 billion. Through the I-CASH unclaimed property program, he has returned more than $2.5 billion in assets to constituents. He says he worked to make sure insurance companies pay life insurance benefits to the intended recipients.

items.text: He launched Illinois Secure Choice, a retirement savings program for private-sector workers who do not have access to an employer-sponsored plan. He made changes to the Bright Start college savings program, which as of 2023 had earned a Gold Rating from Morningstar for five consecutive years. He assumed leadership of a multi-state ABLE alliance, allowing parents to save for children with blindness or disabilities without jeopardizing their federal disability benefits.
